title: Reflexivity and Eberlein Smulian

items.title: Reflexive iff unit ball weakly compact
items.strategy: J_X identifies the weak topology with the relative weak-star topology on J_X(X). Surjectivity transfers Alaoglu compactness. Conversely the compact image of B_X is weak-star closed and Goldstine dense in B_X**; hence equal. Intended relative costs are BPI forward and HB through Goldstine in the converse. Batch 1 now supplies matching interfaces but flags inherited stronger AC and incomplete closure; those intended costs are not verified implemented costs.
items.statement: For a real or complex Banach space X, J_X is onto if and only if its closed unit ball is compact in sigma(X,X*).

items.title: A banach space is reflexive iff its dual is reflexive
items.strategy: If J_X is onto, represent F in X*** by F composed with J_X. Conversely J_X(X) is closed by completeness, and any annihilator F is evaluation by f in X*; vanishing on all J_Xx forces f=0, hence F=0. Annihilator separation proves density. HB plus inherited countable-choice closedness; no Alaoglu is needed.
items.statement: For a real or complex Banach X, X is reflexive iff X* is reflexive.

items.title: Closed subspaces of reflexive spaces are reflexive
items.strategy: For y** compose with restriction X*->Y*. Reflexivity represents the composite by x. Annihilating Y-perp forces x in Y; surjectivity of restriction then proves y**=J_Yx. HB supplies extension/separation; no compactness shortcut is required.
items.statement: Every norm-closed linear subspace Y of a real or complex reflexive Banach space X is reflexive.

items.title: Quotients of reflexive spaces are reflexive
items.strategy: Identify (X/Y)* with Y-perp, extend a functional on Y-perp to X* using HB, represent it by x, and verify its quotient representative is x+Y. Do not assert that the quotient map carries the closed unit ball onto the quotient closed unit ball.
items.statement: If X is a real or complex reflexive Banach space and Y is a closed linear subspace, X/Y is reflexive.

items.title: Reflexivity of lp for one less p less infinity
items.strategy: Apply the real representation theorem at p and its conjugate q and verify the composite is J_Lp, using the bilinear integral pairing. Preserve the complex-scalar scope obligation in the notes rather than silently treating the real supplier as complex.
items.statement: Under the countable-choice hypothesis of the published scalar duality theorem, real Lp(mu) is reflexive on any measure space for 1<p<infinity. The complex extension remains a separate open obligation, not supplied by the real theorem.

items.title: Relative weak compactness and three sequential notions
items.strategy: Define all notions before their equivalence. A cluster point is an indexed-sequence cluster point, not an unspecified accumulation point of a finite range.
items.statement: For A in Banach X, relative weak compactness means weak closure in X is weakly compact; relative weak sequential compactness means every sequence in A has a weakly convergent subsequence with limit in X; relative weak countable compactness means every sequence in A has a weak cluster point in X (every neighborhood contains infinitely many indexed terms). Absolute versions require the limits or cluster points in A. Empty A satisfies the three relative conditions.

items.title: Eberlein smulian separable reduction
items.strategy: Enumerate rational (Gaussian rational in the complex case) finite linear combinations. Hahn-Banach makes restriction X*->Y* onto; thus both weak topologies have the same finite-coordinate tests. Convex norm closure equals weak closure. This reduction alone does not prove Eberlein-Smulian.
items.statement: For a sequence in X, its closed scalar span Y is a separable Banach subspace. Its weak topology is the relative weak topology inherited from X, and Y is weakly closed.

items.title: Eberlein smulian metrization on the relevant dual ball
items.strategy: Choose norming functionals on a countable dense subset of the unit sphere. Their evaluations separate points; compact-to-Hausdorff identifies the topologies on K. This does not metrize all of Y or all weak compact sets in nonseparable spaces. The design title refers to a dual ball, so exact Whitley reconciliation remains open.
items.statement: A weakly compact subset K of a separable normed space Y is weakly metrizable: a countable norming family in Y* gives a continuous injection of K into a countable scalar product, hence a homeomorphism onto its image.

items.title: Eberlein smulian
items.strategy: BLOCKED: recover and read Whitley pp.116–118 in full. The two existing lemmas only close the compact-to-subsequence direction. Add the recursive bidual closure/norming construction before this theorem; the current deps are necessary but not sufficient and must not be certified.
items.statement: For a subset A of a real or complex Banach space, relative weak compactness, relative weak sequential compactness, and relative weak countable compactness are equivalent.

items.title: Reflexive iff every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence
items.strategy: Apply Eberlein-Smulian to the closed unit ball; use weak closedness of that ball and rescale bounded sequences. Blocked with Eberlein-Smulian.
items.statement: A Banach space is reflexive iff every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence in the space.

items.title: Schur property
items.strategy: Definition concerns sequences only; it does not identify the weak and norm topologies.
items.statement: A Banach space has the Schur property when every weakly convergent sequence converges in norm.

items.title: Ell one has the schur property
items.strategy: BLOCKED full-text gliding-hump source verification. From weak nullity and norms bounded away from zero, choose a subsequence and successive finite blocks with head and tail errors small. One bounded scalar phase sequence norms the selected blocks and contradicts weak nullity. Do not choose a different functional for every subsequence term.
items.statement: Real and complex ell-one have the Schur property.

items.title: Ell one is not reflexive
items.strategy: Coordinate unit vectors have mutual distance 2. A weakly convergent subsequence would converge in norm by Schur, impossible.
items.statement: The Banach space ell-one is not reflexive.

items.title: Uniformly convex banach space
items.strategy: State the unit-ball version; distinguish it from strict convexity and from invariance under equivalent renorming.
items.statement: A Banach space is uniformly convex if for each epsilon in (0,2] there is delta>0 such that ||x||,||y||<=1 and ||x-y||>=epsilon imply ||(x+y)/2||<=1-delta.

items.title: Uniform convexity gives unique asymptotic centers
items.strategy: BLOCKED: verify a full proof of existence and uniqueness, with the radius-zero case, a bounded minimizing sequence, and the midpoint estimate. Neither Brezis Theorem 3.31 nor its norming-slice proof supplies this result. Retain the requested result; do not substitute the theorem it was meant to support.
items.statement: For a bounded sequence in a uniformly convex Banach space, the asymptotic radius function r(y)=limsup_n||x_n-y|| has a unique minimizer on each nonempty closed convex subset.

items.title: Milman pettis
items.strategy: Brezis Theorem 3.31: for z in S_X**, choose a norm-one functional almost norming z and a small weak-star slice of B_X**. Goldstine supplies x in the slice. A hypothetical z outside Jx+epsilon B_X** allows a second Goldstine point in the slice farther than epsilon from x, contradicting uniform convexity. Thus J_X(B_X) is norm dense in B_X**, and completeness makes it closed. For complex scalars use real parts. This proof does not dispose of the separately required asymptotic-center lemma.
items.statement: Every real or complex uniformly convex Banach space is reflexive.

items.title: Bishop phelps
items.strategy: BLOCKED support-cone proof. The complex general-convex statement is not asserted. Any complex unit-ball specialization must be justified using the real-part correspondence.
items.statement: For every nonempty closed bounded convex subset C of a real Banach X, the continuous linear functionals attaining their supremum on C are norm dense in X*. In particular norm-attaining functionals are dense for the unit ball.

items.title: Separable dual implies separable primal
items.strategy: Handle X={0}. For a dense sequence f_n choose x_n in the unit ball with |f_n(x_n)|>=||f_n||/2 (take x_n=0 when f_n=0). Any functional annihilating their span has arbitrarily small norm by approximation with f_n. HB annihilator separation gives density; rational or Gaussian rational span gives countability.
items.statement: Under countable choice, if the continuous dual of a real or complex normed space X is norm separable, then X is norm separable.

items.title: Separable reflexive space has separable dual
items.strategy: J_X identifies X** with X, making X** separable; apply the preceding theorem to X*. Separability of X alone does not suffice.
items.statement: Under countable choice, a separable reflexive Banach space has separable dual.

The uniform-convexity corollary must cite this item; exact scalar inequalities, Holder/Minkowski IDs, and full-text backing remain to be audited.

items.strategy: The linearity argument is finite scalar algebra and uniqueness. Continuity awaits the coefficient-space lemma described in notes.
items.statement: A Schauder basis (e_n) in a real or complex Banach X is a sequence such that every x has a unique expansion x=sum_n a_n e_n converging in norm in the fixed order. Define e_n*(x)=a_n. Coordinate linearity follows from uniqueness; boundedness is not part of the definition.

items.title: Approximation property and bounded approximation property
items.strategy: Explicitly define finite-rank as finite-dimensional image and include K empty. A sequence of approximants is not required in a nonseparable space.
items.statement: AP: for every norm-compact K subset X and epsilon>0 there is a bounded finite-rank operator T:X->X with sup_K||Tx-x||<epsilon. Lambda-BAP additionally requires ||T||<=lambda uniformly in K,epsilon; BAP means some finite lambda exists.

items.title: Pointwise convergent uniformly bounded operators converge uniformly on compact sets
items.strategy: The limit is linear and ||T||<=M by taking limits. A finite delta-net of K reduces the estimate to finitely many convergence thresholds plus 2M delta. Handle M=0 separately; no choice family of arbitrary points is needed after choosing one finite net.
items.statement: If T_n:X->Y are bounded linear maps, sup_n||T_n||=M<infinity, and T_nx->Tx for all x, then convergence is uniform on each norm-compact K subset X.

items.title: Unconditional convergence equivalences
items.strategy: Mueger A.4: failure of finite-tail control constructs disjoint bad blocks, then a divergent permutation/subseries; choose least finite-set codes to avoid unspecified choices here. Finite-tail control makes the ordinary partial sums Cauchy and controls the finite-subset net by comparison with that limit. Split Re/Im positive/negative scalar tests to bound sum |f(x_n)| by four times the tail bound. HB norming then proves multiplier Cauchyness. Completeness gives limits. Read A.4 in the alternate short notes; its net-completeness appeal can be replaced by the explicit ordinary partial-sum argument.
items.statement: For a series in a real or complex Banach space, the following are equivalent: all rearrangements converge; all rearrangements converge to the same sum; the finite-subset sum net converges; finite sums outside a sufficiently large finite set are uniformly small; every subseries converges; every bounded scalar multiplier series converges.

items.statement: For a Schauder basis (e_n), the space E of scalar sequences a for which sum a_n e_n converges is Banach in ||a||_E=sup_N||sum_{n<=N}a_ne_n||. The summation map E->X is a bounded linear bijection.
items.strategy: Prove coordinates of an E-Cauchy sequence converge by continuity of coordinates on each finite span. For one epsilon fix a sufficiently close E-sequence a^k and then a tail index for its convergent series. Finite blocks of the coordinatewise limit differ from those of a^k by at most 2epsilon; hence its series is Cauchy. Pass finite-sum inequalities to the limit to obtain convergence in E. Uniqueness/existence of the basis expansion gives bijectivity. No coordinate functional on X is assumed bounded. BLOCKED independent full-source verification of this repair.
